inventory.visualPurpose: The AUTONOMIC/SOMATIC overview schematic (the section's single figure — the classic autonomic nervous system receptor map)
inventory.sourceFigureDescription: The section's entire figure: a left-to-right schematic of the AUTONOMIC division (subdivided Parasympathetic and Sympathetic) and the SOMATIC division. The CNS column at the left (Brainstem above, Spinal cord below) gives off three pathways. PARASYMPATHETIC: 'Preganglionic neuron (long)' → ganglion near the organ (ACh on Nn) → 'Postganglionic neuron (short)' → ACh on 'M₁, M₂, M₃' → 'Smooth muscle, gland cells, nerve terminals, cardiac muscle'. SYMPATHETIC: 'Preganglionic neuron (short)' → the 'Sympathetic chain' (ACh on Nn) → 'Postganglionic neuron (long)' → NE on 'α1, α2, β1, β2' → 'Smooth muscle, gland cells, nerve terminals, cardiac muscle'; a cholinergic sympathetic fiber → ACh on 'M₃' → 'Sweat glands'; a dopaminergic branch → D on 'D1' → 'Renal vasculature smooth muscle'; and the 'Adrenal gland (medulla)' limb — directly innervated by the preganglionic fiber (ACh on Nn), secreting Epi + NE into the 'Blood (catecholamine transmission)' onto 'α1, α2, β1, β2' at 'Cardiac muscle, vessels'. SOMATIC: the 'Voluntary motor nerve' (single neuron) → ACh on 'Nm' at the 'Neuromuscular junction' → 'Skeletal muscle'. Three footnote lines below the figure: 'Pelvic splanchnic nerves and CNs III, VII, IX, and X are part of the parasympathetic nervous system.'; 'Adrenal medulla is directly innervated by preganglionic sympathetic fibers.'; 'Sweat glands are part of the sympathetic pathway but are innervated by cholinergic fibers (sympathetic nervous system results in a “chold” sweat).' VECTOR LINE ART (pdfimages: zero raster rows) — path-drawn nerves/organs with typeset labels.
